name: Fermi Inc. (Fermi America)
headquarters: Dallas, Texas, USA (1845 Woodall Rodgers Freeway, Suite 1100 — per the 31 August 2026 8-K; the company website still lists 620 S. Taylor Street, Amarillo)
employees: 35 full-time at 31 December 2025 (Form 10-K); no later count disclosed
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Fermi America is a pre-revenue, Nasdaq-listed developer of one asset — Project Matador, a behind-the-meter 'private grid' AI campus on a 99-year Texas Tech University System ground lease in Carson County, Texas — that has landed roughly 1.5 GW of gas turbines, permitted 6 GW of gas generation and filed for four Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, but as of 13 August 2026 has energised nothing, holds one binding but conditional tenant lease (TensorWave, 222 MW), and carries going-concern language in its latest 10-Q; whether the TensorWave lease closes with project financing by its 30 September 2026 deadline is the single fact that decides the next twelve months.

BACKGROUND. Fermi LLC was formed on 10 January 2025 by former US Energy Secretary Rick Perry and Toby Neugebauer and converted to Fermi Inc., a Texas corporation, at its IPO: 37,375,000 shares at USD 21.00 (including the full over-allotment), first trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on 1 October 2025 with a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange, USD 745.6 million of net proceeds per the cash-flow statement. The campus plan grew from 'up to 11 GW' at the IPO to 'up to 17 GW' after the TCEQ issued a final air permit for about 6 GW of gas generation on 25 February 2026 and the company filed for a further 5 GW in March. The record since the IPO is one of contraction rather than delivery: the investment-grade 'First Tenant' that signed a letter of intent and a USD 150 million advance-in-aid-of-construction agreement terminated it on 11 December 2025 without drawing funds; the founding CEO was removed on 17 April 2026 and terminated for cause on 30 April, then ran a consent solicitation and sued; the CFO resigned; the share price fell from a USD 36.99 high on 2 October 2025 to USD 4.47 on 9 April 2026 and closed at USD 5.12 on 4 September 2026 (market capitalisation about USD 3.3 billion). FY2025 net loss was USD 486.4 million (largely non-cash), the first half of 2026 lost USD 214.5 million, and cash plus restricted cash stood at USD 91.7 million on 30 June 2026 before USD 431.25 million of 5.00% convertible notes closed in July. The Q2 2026 quarter delivered the five '90-day objectives' the new chairman had set: a binding lease with TensorWave, a permanent CEO (Lee McIntire, from 11 August 2026), a 2.6 GW build-own-operate-transfer framework with Hillcore Energy Capital, contractor relationships with Primoris and TSK, and three Siemens SGT6-5000F turbines landed at the Port of Houston. Per company filings and releases; the price record per Yahoo Finance and StockAnalysis.
ecosystemRole: The generation-first campus in this corpus: where the F7 landlords buy powered land and wait for the utility, Fermi builds its own power plant behind the fence and treats the utility — Xcel Energy's Southwestern Public Service, contracted for up to 200 MW — as the supplement. It is a buyer of Siemens Energy and GE Vernova turbines, an EPC customer of Primoris and TSK, a prospective owner of four AP1000s that Westinghouse, Hyundai E&C and Doosan are lined up to deliver, a 20-year lessee of Mobile Power Solutions' TM2500 fleet, and a landlord whose only signed tenant is an AMD-GPU neocloud. Reporters benchmark it against Crusoe's Abilene Stargate campus, Vantage's Frontier and VoltaGrid's behind-the-meter supply to Oracle; in this corpus its nearest relatives are Intersect Power's energy parks on the buyer side and the AIDC developers on the landlord side.

productsAndServices.name: Private-grid powered AI data-center capacity at Project Matador (the core product)
productsAndServices.category: Build-to-suit and turnkey data-center leasing on a behind-the-meter campus
productsAndServices.description: Fermi describes Project Matador as 'a utility-scale and utility-grade private-grid powered campus for AI-centric customers' and expects revenue from long-term leases of build-to-suit or turnkey data centers, powered shells and ground leases, with rent 'based on reserved power capacity expressed in kilowatts per month' plus fixed and variable power charges passed through to tenants (Q2 2026 10-Q). The plan is 'up to approximately 15 million square feet of AI-ready hyperscale compute' (10-K; 18 million square feet in third-party accounts). The company was pre-revenue at 30 June 2026.
highlights: The one signed lease: TensorWave TEX1, LLC (a subsidiary of TensorWave Inc., an AMD-GPU neocloud) with Fermi Campus 1 LLC, signed 9 August 2026 — 222 MW of total facility power, about 311,496 square feet on about 250 acres, four data halls and a network hall, a 15-year initial term from final-phase commencement with two five-year renewals, about USD 6.5 billion of contracted revenue, and an expansion option to 650 MW that must be energised by 31 December 2028; delivery in phases from late 2027 into Q1 2028 (10-Q Note 9; IR release).

The lease is binding but conditional: effectiveness requires closing 'on or before September 30, 2026 (subject to extension)' with board approvals, 'requisite project guaranties' and project-level financing; either side may terminate if the conditions fail (10-Q). The original 10 August release said the obligations were expected 'to be guaranteed by one of the global leaders in AI'; the corrected release removed the line, and no guarantor had been named by 5 September 2026 (Pacific Software Ventures; IR release).

The lease that was not: an investment-grade 'First Tenant' signed a letter of intent on 19 September 2025 and a USD 150 million advance-in-aid-of-construction agreement on 3 November 2025, then terminated it on 11 December 2025 after exclusivity lapsed, with no funds drawn (8-K 12 December 2025). Business Insider reported the tenant was Amazon; Fermi 'categorically' denied it (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, 17 December 2025).

Pipeline in the company's words: 'seven potential tenants and twelve potential joint venture partners' (9 July 2026 offering memorandum excerpts); 'roughly a dozen prospective customers and strategic partners' (CCO, 13 August 2026 call). Fortune reported the company 'failed to secure anchor tenant by March deadline' in 2026.

Implied economics, third-party arithmetic: about USD 162.70 per kW-month on total facility power for the TensorWave lease (Pacific Software Ventures) — a calculation on the headline figures, not a disclosed rate.
productsAndServices.positioning: Company framing: 'the only private grid campus of its kind with over 2GW of secured long lead time generation assets, an approved ~6GW Clean Air Permit' (March 2026 release) and, per the chairman on 13 August 2026, 'There is no site we know of that has equipment and the ability to deliver 4.8 gigawatts during this time period'. The 10-K names no competitor by name (generic classes: data-center developers, powered-shell and colocation providers, IPPs, utilities, hyperscaler self-build). Reporters benchmark it against Crusoe's Stargate Abilene (200 MW live in 15 months), Vantage's Frontier campus north of Abilene and Meta's Hyperion (Distilled, April 2026); Barclays is reported to cite VoltaGrid's 2.3 GW of behind-the-meter supply to Oracle's Stargate as the comparator.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct long-term leases to AI tenants (build-to-suit, turnkey, powered shell or ground lease); power sold to tenants as fixed and variable charges under a modified net lease; the Hillcore block would be bought under long-term power purchase agreements and resold to tenants.
targetSegments: Enterprise compute operators and joint-venture partners (company pipeline language)
productsAndServices.roadmap: 200 MW of initial commercial power 'over the next six months' from 13 August 2026 and about 1.5 GW over 18–24 months, 'subject to binding customer agreements and approvals' (Q2 release); first 210 MW available 1 July 2027 and 640 MW nameplate by Q4 2027 (COO prepared remarks); TensorWave building late 2027 to Q1 2028; 4.8 GW 'within about 30 months' including Hillcore (17 August 2026 explainer). The company website still says 'first power online in 2026'.

productsAndServices.name: Project Matador site — land, water, gas, fibre and the utility tie
productsAndServices.category: Powered land and site infrastructure (Carson County, Texas)
productsAndServices.description: A 99-year ground lease dated 14 May 2025 with the Texas Tech University System covers about 5,236 acres (4,523 acres commenced in September 2025; a 713-acre tract awaits a land exchange with the National Nuclear Security Administration), adjacent to the Department of Energy's Pantex Plant north-east of Amarillo; with adjacent purchases and options the company describes 'approximately 8,400 acres in the aggregate' (Q2 2026 10-Q; the 10-K said about 7,570). Phase 0 site enablement was 'substantially complete' by February 2026: more than 11 miles of perimeter fence, about 5 miles of high-pressure gas pipeline, 7 miles of water lines with a 2-million-gallon tank, about 300 acres prepared and the 'bathtub' excavations for six SGT-800 power islands (10-K; Q2 release).
highlights: Lease economics as published by the Amarillo Tribune from the lease: base rent USD 1.2 million in year one rising to USD 3.5 million in year five then 3% a year; 1% of appraised value on the first USD 3 billion of improvements and 0.5% above; 1% of gross power sales; 25% of gross groundwater sales; a USD 4.75 million initial contribution and at least USD 1 million a year to an Excellence Fund; the university system estimates about USD 196 million a year at full build. The 30 March 2026 Collaboration Agreement added USD 2 million of prepaid rent and a USD 9 million escrow due 31 December 2026 (10-K).

Water: City of Amarillo agreement for up to 2.5 million gallons a day (framework to 10 MGD per the 10-K; 5.5 MGD per the Tribune), approved 4–1 in October 2025 at double the industrial rate with Fermi funding all infrastructure; a 30-year groundwater lease over about 2,542 acres (Q1 2026 10-Q); MVM EGI hybrid dry-wet cooling agreement (December 2025) claimed to cut water use by 80%. Amarillo's May 2026 moratorium proposal does not reach the campus, which is outside city limits.

Gas: a firm supply arrangement with Energy Transfer (9 October 2025) scalable to about 300,000 MMBtu/day, with a planned dedicated Waha interconnect; the initial 1 GW load needs about 175,000 MMBtu/day (10-K). Fibre: FiberLight, AT&T and Optimum corridors (prospectus).

Grid: the SPS electric service agreement for up to 200 MW over a 115 kV system (see the utility entry below). The Texas Tech lease requires subtenant approval above 200 MW per the S-11 as reported by the Amarillo Tribune.
productsAndServices.positioning: Carson County's 10-year property-tax abatement and reinvestment zone (October 2025) price the campus at USD 3 per square foot of improvements plus USD 2,500–2,750 per MW a year with a 600-job commitment (Amarillo Tribune). The site's distinguishing claims are permitted generation and secured turbines rather than a grid queue position.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Held under the ground lease by Fermi subsidiaries; sublet to tenants and, under the Hillcore framework, about 400 acres subleased to the power partner.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Additional TCEQ air permit for about 5 GW filed 27 March 2026 (pending); the Part 3 site-specific nuclear application due 31 December 2026; NNSA land exchange for 713 acres pending.

productsAndServices.name: Behind-the-meter gas generation — the owned turbine fleet and the Hillcore power center
productsAndServices.category: On-site generation (simple cycle first, combined cycle later)
productsAndServices.description: Fermi owns or leases four turbine fleets, none energised as of 13 August 2026: six Siemens Energy SGT-800s with six HRSGs and an SST-600 steam turbine (about 296 MW simple cycle, 396 MW combined per the Q2 deck; 478 MW ISO combined per the company site), bought from MAD Energy in the 'Firebird Acquisition' and financed by a USD 165 million Beal Bank/CSG facility; three Siemens SGT6-5000F F-class units (728 MW simple cycle, 1,042 MW combined) under a 28 January 2026 equipment purchase agreement at a fixed price of about USD 324.4 million, financed by MUFG's USD 500 million warehouse and landed at the Port of Houston in July 2026; three secondary-market GE Frame 6B units with a steam turbine (about 116 MW) from the Bayonne, New Jersey plant, refurbished in Houston; and seven GE TM2500 mobile units (157.5 MW nameplate, 126–132 MW at site elevation) under a 20-year lease with Mobile Power Solutions whose pick-up was deferred to July–September 2027. Further SGT-800s are 'on order and expected to be delivered in 2028' (Q2 2026 10-Q; deck; 10-K).
highlights: Time-to-power as the company tables it: TM2500 two months, GE 6B eight months, SGT-800 fifteen months, SGT6-5000F twenty-two months (Q2 2026 investor presentation) — the fleet is sequenced so that the smallest, fastest units carry the first tenant.

Phase 1 is all simple cycle: about 200 MW of SPS grid power plus roughly 132 MW of TM2500s, 114 MW of GE 6Bs and 300 MW of SGT-800s; the COO's 13 August 2026 remarks put 'the first 210 megawatts available July 1, 2027' and '640 megawatts of nameplate capacity by the fourth quarter of 2027'. Phase 2 adds the HRSGs and steam turbines (combined cycle), more SGT-800s in 2028, solar and batteries; the F-class units carry '28/29 power delivery objectives' (prepared remarks; 10-Q).

Hillcore Power Center (framework agreement 11 August 2026, definitive documents within about 90 days): Hillcore Energy Capital — owned by the Hillcore Group and the JV Driver Group — would finance, build, own and operate about 2.6 GW (about 2.5 GW of gas plus about 100 MW of solar and storage) on about 400 subleased acres, with Fermi as anchor offtaker under long-term PPAs (take-or-pay on at least 50% of tenant load per the 10-Q), a first block of about 350–360 MW within 24 months of notice to proceed, and a 10-year Fermi option to buy at fair market value; the company says it 'doubles' power to market to about 4.8 GW over about 30 months (wire release; 17 August 2026 explainer).

Contractors: Primoris Services Corporation for Phase One balance of plant on the SGT-800s; TSK Electrónica y Electricidad USA for early-works and fast-start engineering on the F-class units (25 June 2026); Relevant Power Solutions leading the GE 6B and TM2500 deployment (COO remarks); Parkhill and Lee Lewis Construction announced as construction partners in August 2025 (newsroom index; POWER Magazine).

Fuel and equipment obligations: a Siemens Rated Capacity Agreement of up to about USD 240 million over 10 years on the F-class units; USD 142.6 million of remaining Siemens purchase commitments at 30 June 2026; a 2.5% net-profits interest to MAD Energy on the first 1 GW capped at USD 100 million NPV; TM2500 rent through 2045 (10-Q).
productsAndServices.positioning: The fleet is the company's proof of scarcity: 'over 2GW of secured long lead time generation assets' at the TCEQ permit and 'total landed: 1.5 GW' by Q2 2026, against an industry turbine queue the company and its critics both describe as years long. The counter-claim, from Cleanview's satellite series and Distilled, is that no building had risen by April 2026 and the project was at least a year behind its IPO schedule.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owned by Fermi subsidiaries and financed asset by asset (MUFG, Beal/CSG, Keystone); the Hillcore block would be third-party owned with Fermi as anchor buyer; output sold to tenants as pass-through power charges.
targetSegments: Project Matador tenants only — the generation is captive to the campus
productsAndServices.roadmap: 200 MW grid power over the next six months (Q2 release); simple-cycle first power 2027; combined-cycle conversion and 2028 SGT-800 deliveries; Hillcore first block within 24 months of NTP; total generation 'up to 11 GW … expandable up to approximately 17 GW' subject to land and TCEQ permits (10-K).

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear programme — four Westinghouse AP1000 units under a combined license application
productsAndServices.description: Fermi America filed Parts 1 and 2 of a combined license application for four Westinghouse AP1000 reactors (AP1000 DCD Revision 19) on 17 June and 20 August 2025; the NRC accepted them for review on 5 September 2025 under dockets 052-00051 to 052-00054 — the first large light-water COLA accepted since Turkey Point 6 and 7 in 2009 (POWER Magazine). Part 3, the site-specific portion, is targeted for 31 December 2026. Fermi is the first applicant in the NRC's applicant-prepared environmental impact statement pilot: the Federal Register scoping notice issued 20 March 2026, the applicant's draft EIS was completed in July 2026, and the NRC targets a final EIS in December 2026 (NRC COL page; ANS). The 10-K describes about 6.0 GW of nuclear across two islands at full build; the Q2 2026 10-Q schedules one unit in each of 2033, 2034, 2035 and 2036 (the first unit slipped about a year).
highlights: Partners on the record: Westinghouse (licensing support, August 2025); Hyundai Engineering & Construction (MOU July 2025; FEED completed July 2026; 'potential EPC pathway' per the 11 February 2026 release); Doosan Enerbility (forging readiness agreement); ASP Isotopes and Quantum Leap Energy (HALEU MOU); KHNP and Samsung C&T named by World Nuclear News.

Funding: applications to DOE's Office of Energy Dominance Financing, the Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program and the Texas HB14 Advanced Nuclear Completion Fund; the company expects to monetise 45J, 45Q, 45V and 48C credits 'to the extent available' (10-Q). Total all-phase capital need is stated at 'USD 70 billion to USD 90 billion'.
Small modular reactors appear in the master plan but remain 'undecided' (ANS, April 2026); the site's progress page assigns 4.4 GW to 'Westinghouse AP1000s + SMRs'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Nuclear is the campus's long-dated differentiator and its political banner (the site is styled the 'President Donald J. Trump Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus' in NRC and trade-press accounts); no tenant, PPA or financing is attached to it, and construction cannot begin before a COL.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not yet a product — a licensing programme; output would be sold to campus tenants.
targetSegments: Federal and state nuclear funding programmes
productsAndServices.roadmap: Part 3 by 31 December 2026; final EIS December 2026; mandatory hearing and Commission decision undated; construction about five years after a COL; first unit 2033 (10-Q).

productsAndServices.name: Utility interconnection and renewables — the SPS electric service agreement, solar and storage
productsAndServices.description: On 5 December 2025 Fermi executed an electric service agreement with Southwestern Public Service Company, Xcel Energy's Texas–New Mexico utility, for up to 200 MW over SPS's 115 kV system: the release said 86 MW would begin in January 2026 and ramp to 200 MW; the 10-K restated the 86 MW as 'expected to be energized in the second half of 2026', the incremental 114 MW targeted for year-end 2026 and 'contractually' by 1 October 2027; the Q2 2026 release still describes 'working with Xcel Energy toward 200 MW onsite power'. Solar and batteries appear in the master plan and in the Hillcore block (about 100 MW); the progress page assigns 1 GW to 'Xcel Interconnect, Solar & Battery' and says the company is 'vetting Solar and Battery Partners'.
highlights: SPS sits in SPP, not ERCOT, so the campus is outside the Texas large-load verification directive the governor issued in August 2026 — the CEO's op-ed says the directive 'does not negatively impact Project Matador'.

No PUCT or SPP interconnection docket for the campus was located by this research; the 10-K conditions energisation on 'regulatory approvals, SPS interconnection work schedules'. Xcel did not name Fermi on its Q2 2026 earnings call.
On the FY2025 call the then-CEO put the value of an extension to the Xcel agreement at about USD 8–10 million (Investing.com transcript summary).
productsAndServices.positioning: Grid power is the bridge, not the model: 200 MW is under 2% of the permitted campus, and the same figure is the first-phase 'commercial power' the company promised within six months of August 2026.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Retail service from SPS under applicable tariffs; passed through to tenants.
targetSegments: First-phase tenant energisation before on-site generation is live
productsAndServices.roadmap: 86 MW in H2 2026; 200 MW by 1 October 2027 contractually; solar and battery partner selection undated.

recentDevelopments.headline: CEO op-ed: the Texas governor's data-center interconnection directive 'does not negatively impact Project Matador'

recentDevelopments.headline: Fermi discloses a 30 July 2026 subpoena from the US District Court for the Eastern District of New York and a 3 August SEC voluntary-production request concerning Project Matador and 'certain former members of management'; shares fall about 4%

relationships.via: Southwestern Public Service Company electric service agreement (115 kV)
relationships.note: Xcel Energy's SPS utility supplies the campus's only grid power: up to 200 MW over its 115 kV system under a 5 December 2025 electric service agreement.
relationships.context: The release said 86 MW would begin in January 2026 and ramp to 200 MW; the FY2025 10-K restated the 86 MW as expected 'in the second half of 2026', with the incremental 114 MW targeted for year-end 2026 and contractually due by 1 October 2027. The Q2 2026 earnings release still describes 'working with Xcel Energy toward 200 MW onsite power', so no grid power had been energised by mid-August 2026. Xcel's Texas–New Mexico president Adrian Rodriguez was quoted in the release; Xcel did not name Fermi on its Q2 2026 earnings call, and the company's Xcel dossier records the agreement as the only named SPS data-center contract and the smallest tier of its pipeline slide. No PUCT or SPP interconnection docket for the campus was located.

relationships.via: SGT-800 and SGT6-5000F gas turbines; Rated Capacity Agreement
relationships.note: Siemens Energy is the campus's principal turbine vendor: six SGT-800s with HRSGs and an SST-600 (via the Firebird Acquisition from MAD Energy) and three SGT6-5000F F-class units bought directly under a 28 January 2026 equipment purchase agreement.
relationships.context: The Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs describe the F-class purchase at a fixed price of about USD 324.4 million, financed by MUFG's warehouse facility, with a Siemens Rated Capacity Agreement of up to about USD 240 million over ten years and USD 142.6 million of remaining purchase commitments at 30 June 2026. The SGT-800s arrived at the Port of Houston in February 2026 and the F-class units in July 2026; a September 2025 letter of intent for '1.1 GW F-class' and a nuclear collaboration appears in the company's newsroom index. None of the units was energised at 13 August 2026.

relationships.scale: 3 Frame 6B (~116 MW) + 7 TM2500 (157.5 MW nameplate, leased)
relationships.via: Secondary-market Frame 6B units; TM2500 mobile turbines leased from Mobile Power Solutions
relationships.note: GE Vernova equipment makes up the fast end of the fleet: three refurbished Frame 6B units bought from the Bayonne, New Jersey plant and seven TM2500 mobile turbines under a 20-year lease with Mobile Power Solutions.
relationships.context: The Q2 2026 investor presentation tables the 6Bs at 116 MW with an eight-month time to power and foundations poured, and the TM2500s at 126 MW on site (157.5 MW nameplate) with a two-month time to power but held by the lessor until pick-up between 1 July and 30 September 2027. The 6B purchase (an USD 18.0 million equipment purchase agreement of 26 June 2025) is the subject of Bayonne Plant Holding's suit in the District of New Jersey over site-restoration claims. GE Vernova itself is not a contracting party in the filings — the units were bought second-hand and leased through a third party.

relationships.via: Phase One balance-of-plant EPC for the six SGT-800s
relationships.note: Primoris Services Corporation is the balance-of-plant contractor for Phase One (the six SGT-800 power islands), named in the Q2 2026 earnings release among the 'deepened relationships with contractors Primoris, TSK'.
relationships.context: The company's fourth 90-day objective was contractor relationships; the earnings release names Primoris for Phase One balance of plant and TSK for the F-class early works. Contract value and scope beyond 'balance of plant' are not disclosed.

relationships.note: Business Insider reported that Amazon was the investment-grade 'First Tenant' whose USD 150 million advance-in-aid-of-construction agreement was terminated on 11 December 2025; Fermi and its then-CEO 'categorically' denied the report.
relationships.context: The 8-K of 12 December 2025 identifies the counterparty only as an investment-grade tenant that signed a letter of intent on 19 September 2025 and the agreement on 3 November 2025, and terminated it after exclusivity lapsed with no funds drawn. Reuters (via Yahoo Finance) carried the Business Insider attribution and Fermi's denial; Amazon did not comment. This dossier records the link as reported and denied, not as a relationship; the Amazon dossier carries nothing on Fermi.

relationships.note: Reporters benchmark Project Matador's schedule against Crusoe's Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas, which put 200 MW online in about 15 months.
relationships.context: Distilled's April 2026 analysis compares Fermi with Crusoe's Abilene build (1.2 GW; 200 MW live by September 2025), Vantage's Frontier campus north of Abilene and Meta's Hyperion, and estimates that even with an immediate tenant Fermi could not match Crusoe's pace before May 2027. Fermi's own filings name no competitor.

relationships.note: Vantage's 1.2 GW Frontier campus north of Abilene, begun in September 2025, is the second Texas behind-the-meter campus reporters set against Project Matador.
relationships.context: Same Distilled comparison: Frontier and Stargate Abilene are the two Texas campuses that broke ground in 2025 and had visible buildings by April 2026 while Fermi's satellite record showed site work only. In this corpus Vantage's Frontier is primary-powered by VoltaGrid gas microgrids — the closest structural analogue to Fermi's own private-grid claim.

policyExposure.regime: NRC combined license (10 CFR Part 52) and the applicant-prepared EIS pilot
policyExposure.exposure: The four-unit AP1000 combined license application (dockets 052-00051 to 052-00054) was accepted for review on 5 September 2025; Part 3 is targeted for 31 December 2026 and the NRC targets a final environmental impact statement in December 2026, with the mandatory hearing and Commission decision undated. Construction of the nuclear islands cannot begin before a COL; the 10-Q's reactor schedule (2033–2036) already slipped a year.
policyExposure.mitigation: Fermi is the first applicant in the NRC's pilot for applicant-prepared draft EISs under the amended NEPA process, which the NRC says shortens its review; the applicant's draft EIS was completed in July 2026.

policyExposure.exposure: The final permit for about 6 GW of gas-fired generation issued on 25 February 2026 after a self-imposed construction pause; an application for a further 5 GW was filed on 27 March 2026 and is pending. The 17 GW ambition, and any generation beyond the first 6 GW, depends on the second permit.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company sequenced Phase 0 civil works ahead of the permit and resumed on issuance; the 5 GW application was filed within a month.

policyExposure.regime: Texas large-load interconnection directive (ERCOT) — not applicable to SPS/SPP
policyExposure.exposure: The governor's August 2026 directive requiring ERCOT data-center interconnection verification does not reach the campus, which takes its grid power from SPS in the Southwest Power Pool and generates behind the meter; the CEO's op-ed says it 'does not negatively impact Project Matador'. The 10-K nonetheless conditions SPS energisation on 'regulatory approvals, SPS interconnection work schedules'.

Lupia v. Fermi Inc. (S.D.N.Y. 1:26-cv-00050) alleges Securities Act and Exchange Act violations over tenant-demand disclosures for the 1 October–11 December 2025 class period; a 30 July 2026 subpoena from the Eastern District of New York and a 3 August SEC voluntary-production request concern Project Matador and former management. Four further suits are on the 10-Q: 340 Energy v. Firebird (turbine broker fee, motion to dismiss denied 11 August 2026), Neugebauer v. Fermi (Texas Business Court, seeking to void the 70% bylaw and his removal), Bayonne Plant Holding v. Fermi Equipment Holdco (D.N.J., site restoration) and Peña and Summers v. Fermi and Neugebauer (claims above USD 415 million).
policyExposure.mitigation: The company states there is no allegation of wrongdoing in the subpoena and that it is cooperating; MAD Energy indemnifies the 340 Energy claim.

policyExposure.regime: Federal and Texas nuclear and clean-energy incentives (45J, 45Q, 45V, 48C; DOE Office of Energy Dominance Financing; Texas HB14)
policyExposure.exposure: The 10-Q describes a pre-approval process with the DOE Office of Energy Dominance Financing and applications to the Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program and the Texas Advanced Nuclear Completion Fund, and an expectation of monetising 45J, 45Q, 45V and 48C credits 'to the extent available'. No award is on the record.

policyExposure.regime: Local water and tax agreements (City of Amarillo; Carson County)
policyExposure.exposure: Amarillo's council approved up to 2.5 million gallons a day at double the industrial rate with Fermi funding all infrastructure (4–1, October 2025); a May 2026 proposal for a two-year moratorium on large data centers inside the city does not apply to the campus. Carson County granted a 10-year abatement and reinvestment zone. The Texas Tech lease takes 25% of gross groundwater sales.
policyExposure.mitigation: Hybrid dry-wet cooling (MVM EGI, December 2025) with a company claim of 80% less water than conventional designs; a 30-year groundwater lease over about 2,542 acres.

periods.commentary: The first annual report of a company that listed nine months after formation: every large line is an equity award, a fair-value mark on convertible notes or a charitable gift of units, and the operating outflow is USD 34 million. Consensus did not exist for the period and none is manufactured here. Analyst coverage that has since formed is priced on tenant signings — Stifel cut its target from USD 29 to USD 17 in June 2026 citing contract delays; TipRanks' August 2026 table runs from UBS at USD 6 (Hold) to Citizens at USD 30 (Market Outperform); MarketBeat's 13-analyst consensus of USD 20.67 and StockAnalysis's 8-analyst USD 17.13 disagree with each other on the same date.

financials.commentary: Fiscal year ends 31 December. The Q3 2026 report has no announced date: the IR 'Upcoming Events' page was empty on 5 September 2026 and the filing cadence (Q3 2025 letter 10 November 2025; Q1 2026 release 14 May; Q2 release 13 August, 10-Q the next day) points to a release in the week of 10 November 2026 with the 10-Q due by 16 November under the emerging-growth 45-day deadline. The first annual meeting is 30 October 2026 (record date 31 August). Nearer catalysts: the TensorWave closing deadline of 30 September 2026 (extendable), the Yorkville note's expiry about the same date, Hillcore definitive documents about 90 days from 11 August, the MUFG nine-month test of a lease of at least 400 MW around 10 November, the Keystone approved-customer-agreement deadline of 31 December 2026 and the USD 9 million Texas Tech escrow due the same day. Share price USD 5.12 on 4 September 2026 (all-time high USD 36.99 on 2 October 2025; low USD 4.47 on 9 April 2026); market capitalisation about USD 3.28 billion; short interest 7.69% of float.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Fermi's product is time-to-power rather than land or buildings, and that the company has converted its balance sheet into that claim: about 1.5 GW of turbines landed and 6 GW of gas permitted before any tenant, financed by three equipment lenders at 12–13% and a warehouse line that punishes the absence of a 400 MW lease by November 2026. Basis: the fleet table with time-to-power by unit in the Q2 2026 presentation; the MUFG, Keystone and Beal facility terms in the 8-Ks and 10-Q; the chairman's 'no site we know of that has equipment and the ability to deliver 4.8 gigawatts'.

(High confidence) We assess that the TensorWave lease is a conditional option on the company rather than a contract in force until it closes: effectiveness requires project-level financing, board approvals and a third-party guarantor by 30 September 2026 (extendable), the guarantor line was removed from the release, and the tenant is a venture-backed neocloud whose parent guaranty is the only credit named. Basis: 10-Q Note 9; the two versions of the 10 August release as documented by Pacific Software Ventures; TensorWave's investor list. Collection gap: no 8-K for the lease and no named guarantor by 5 September 2026.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the Hillcore build-own-operate-transfer framework is a capital-substitution move that halves the generation Fermi must fund itself, at the cost of a take-or-pay obligation on at least half of tenant load and a partner that has not yet signed definitive documents. Basis: the framework's structure (Hillcore finances, builds, owns and operates; Fermi buys under long-term PPAs with a 10-year FMV purchase option) against Fermi's USD 91.7 million of cash and 'over $3 billion' of Phase 0–1 capex. The 2.2 GW self-build plus 2.6 GW Hillcore arithmetic that yields '4.8 GW' counts a framework as capacity.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the governance conflict is unresolved rather than finished: the former CEO's consent solicitation is 'suspended', his litigation and the company's counter-suits continue, the 70% bylaw he contests remains, and the 30 October 2026 annual meeting is the first vote under the new board. Basis: the duelling DEFC14A filings, the July 2026 8-Ks, the 10-Q's litigation note and the 31 August 8-K. The two ownership figures — 22.7% in his filing, 'approximately 40%' in the company's — are a dispute about affiliates and dates, not a reconciliation.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the schedule now on the record is 2027 for first on-site power and 2033 for first nuclear power, and that the company's website ('first power online in 2026') and the SPS release ('86 MW beginning January 2026') are stale. Basis: the COO's 13 August 2026 remarks (210 MW on 1 July 2027; 640 MW nameplate by Q4 2027), the 10-K's restatement of the SPS energisation to the second half of 2026, the 10-Q's reactor schedule, and the Cleanview and Distilled satellite record. Indicator: whether the '200 megawatts of initial commercial power over the next six months' (SPS grid power) is energised by February 2027.

(Low confidence) We assess that the AP1000 programme is a licensing asset and a political banner rather than a financeable project on any current horizon: no tenant, PPA, EPC contract or funding award is attached to it, the first unit slipped to 2033 inside a year, and the stated all-phase capital need is USD 70–90 billion for a company capitalised at about USD 3.3 billion. Basis: the NRC docket schedule, the 10-Q's nuclear section and the absence of nuclear-specific financing in any filing. The counter-evidence is real: the COLA is docketed, the EIS pilot is running, Hyundai completed the FEED and Doosan is lined up — the programme is further along than most announced US nuclear builds.

Collection gap: no PUCT or SPP interconnection docket for the SPS agreement; no first-party disclosure of the TensorWave guarantor, the Hillcore definitive agreement or the data-center general contractor; the July 2026 consent tally and the Bayonne and Peña/Summers suits are known only from the 10-Q's summary and mirrors; the Q3 2026 report date is inferred from cadence. INDICATORS TO WATCH: 30 September 2026 — TensorWave closing or extension, with or without a named guarantor; ~9 November 2026 — Hillcore definitive documents; 10 November 2026 — MUFG 400 MW lease test and the probable Q3 report; 30 October 2026 — the first annual meeting and any founder nominations; 31 December 2026 — Keystone approved-customer deadline, Texas Tech escrow, NRC Part 3; H2 2026 — energisation of the 86 MW SPS block, which would be the first watt delivered to the site.
